title: Three consumed contracts and two platform reads of the petition have no dependency row, and two of the three operation names exist in no source
source: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP table rows DP-03, DP-07, DP-08, DP-13, DP-19 and section R5.4 dependency classes; the metadata rows of RWB-S4-E5021-APP (Depends on (build) = RWB-S4-E5021-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON; Contract dependencies = None; Integration dependencies = None; External dependencies = None) and of RWB-S4-E5021-CON (all three None); Architecture v5 slide 19 (rwb-litigation OUT: Partner: issueInstruction (law firm) and Decision: child: approval; IN: events NoticeDelivered and PartnerResultSubmitted) and slide 41; the plan slice list of the legacy key; legacy RWB-E5-021 Depends on FEAT-APD-01
section: Sections 3, 12.2, 12.8 and 13 of both stories, Pattern application and Pinned dependencies; the metadata table and the two fragments
description: The two stories consume five things that no metadata row carries. (1) The D7.5 approval of rwb-decision, whose contract the plan names as RWB-P7-E2013-CON 'Approval routing with the delegation of authority table'. (2) The rwb-case contract that reads the case route state and answers the route fact BANKRUPTCY_PETITION, because the case of record and its route state are P3's and R-LIT-58 moves them. (3) The rwb-partner firm instruction, which Architecture v5 slide 19 names only as 'Partner: issueInstruction (law firm)'. (4) The reference-data read of LOV-LEGAL-TYPE and LOV-LEGAL-STATUS, because DP-07 is not in either story's pattern set while TSD S4 T3.2 makes both lists required for action_type and status. (5) The declared Litigation right of each operation, because DP-08 is not in either story's pattern set and the rights of TSD S4 T6.1 have to be enforced somewhere. The approval contract is a P7 contract story of wave 2, so it is a C dependency that does not block; the case and partner contracts have no CON story in the plan at all and are built against their fakes. Two of the five also have no operation name in any source: the case read, the route fact and the firm instruction request are described only in prose, so their names are carried as the placeholder in both stories. A reader of the metadata alone would conclude that the petition needs only the two platform contracts and its own contract.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5: DP-03 adds H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, DP-07 adds H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON, DP-08 adds H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON and C RWB-P4-E1037-CON, DP-19 adds H RWB-PLT-N001-CON; the patterns applied to both stories are DP03, DP13 and DP19 only; the metadata rows of both stories name no contract, integration or external dependency; Architecture v5 slide 19 gives rwb-litigation IN 'REST GET/POST /legal-actions; GET/POST /hearings' and OUT 'TMP Partner: issueInstruction (law firm) - Comms: child: demand notice - Decision: child: approval' with no path or operation name; the TSD S4 v2 T-A.1 operation inventory holds API-S4-001 to API-S4-005 of rwb-litigation and no operation of rwb-case, rwb-decision or rwb-partner; the Ownership Map publishes no case, approval or partner operation for this key
area: Dependency map and build sequencing, S4 rwb-litigation with P7 rwb-decision, P3 rwb-case, S9 rwb-partner and P4 rwb-access
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P7 rwb-decision, P3 rwb-case and S9 rwb-partner architects and the platform team
proposed: Carry the five as non-blocking consumed rows in the Dependency Map: the approval contract RWB-P7-E2013-CON as a C dependency of wave 2, the case and partner contracts as published contracts built against their fakes, the reference-data contract RWB-P3-E1043-CON as a C dependency, and the declared right of each operation as the edge and guard rule of DP-08; name the case read, the route fact and the instruction request in the case and partner contract stories when they are written, and leave the metadata rows of the plan as they are.

title: The legacy master carries no requirement identifier for RWB-E5-021, so both stories trace to the feature only
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md heading RWB-E5-021 (metadata table: Epic, Module, Feature FEAT-LIT-21, Process, Priority, Depends on FEAT-APD-01, Decision) ; _work/msr/plan/legacy_index.json entry RWB-E5-021 with reqs = [] ; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md row FEAT-LIT-21 ; FSD S4 v3 Requirements served (REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010, none of them naming a bankruptcy petition)
section: Sections 2 and 18 of both stories; the reqs key of both fragments
description: The legacy story RWB-E5-021 carries no REQ identifier: its metadata table names the feature FEAT-LIT-21 and the prerequisite FEAT-APD-01 and no requirement row, the plan's legacy index records an empty requirement list, and the FSD S4 requirements table lists ten requirements of the module whose texts cover notices, the pack, the panel, court tracking, settlement, enforcement, deferral, prescription and proceeds but not the bankruptcy petition. The Epics 3 to 8 specification gives the feature one row and no requirement. Both stories therefore trace to FEAT-LIT-21 and to the L3 process 08 Litigate and enforce, and the requirement column carries the placeholder until the Epics 3 to 8 PRD of the module adds the identifiers. Nothing blocks the build; the exposure is a traceability report that cannot roll the story up to a requirement.
evidence: The metadata table of RWB-E5-021 has seven rows and no requirement row; the legacy index of the run records reqs: [] for the key; FSD S4 v3 'Requirements served' lists REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010 with no petition requirement; the Epics 3 to 8 specification row for FEAT-LIT-21 gives Epic E5, Module S4, Kind User, Primary role Enforcement owner, Systems LIT and Partner portal, Depends on FEAT-APD-01 and no requirement
area: Traceability and requirements, EP05, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: Business analyst, S4 rwb-litigation, with the PRD owner of EP05
proposed: Add one requirement row to the Epics 3 to 8 PRD and to the S4 module trace, covering the petition as a legal action that is taken to the approver at D7.5 and filed through the firm, and rewrite the requirement column of both stories and of their fragments when it exists.

title: The catalogue lists LawsuitFiled on the litigation topic but assigns no story to it, so the filing of a bankruptcy petition is tied to no event
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 19 (rwb-litigation OUT: EVT rwb.litigation.events.v1: LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult) and slide 43 (row: JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult with producers rwb-litigation and consumers rwb-asset and rwb-case); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-09 and the pattern set of this key (DP03, DP13, DP19)
section: Sections 2, 12.3 and 12.4 of both stories; the events_published key of both fragments
description: LawsuitFiled is published on rwb.litigation.events.v1 by the event catalogue and consumes no consumer in the catalogue row, and no story of the plan owns it. The petition is the case type that a court filing produces, so a reader may reasonably expect the filing of a petition to raise LawsuitFiled; but DP-09 is not in either story's pattern set, no outbox row or producer is added by the two stories, and no source states that the petition filing is the event's trigger. Declaring it would put an event into the build that no owner assigned, and omitting it silently would leave an event of the service with no story. Both stories therefore publish nothing and the assignment is recorded here.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 19 'EVT rwb.litigation.events.v1: LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult'; slide 43 lists JudgmentRecorded and AuctionResult with their consumers and gives LawsuitFiled no consumer row; the event catalogue of 30 rows plus four extra rows names no producer story for LawsuitFiled; the plan slice list of the legacy key holds two slices only, an APP and a CON; the patterns applied to both stories are DP03, DP13 and DP19 and none is DP-09
area: Event contract, S4 rwb-litigation with S5 rwb-asset and P3 rwb-case
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the event platform owner and the rwb-case and rwb-asset analysts
proposed: Decide once, in the event catalogue of the service, whether the filing of any legal action raises LawsuitFiled and which story publishes it: if the petition filing is the trigger, assign the event to RWB-S4-E5021-APP and add DP-09 and the outbox row to the story, and if another story owns it, name that story in the catalogue row and keep both petition stories publishing nothing.

title: The D7.5 approval child workflow has no type name, workflow ID or queue registration beyond the queue of rwb-decision
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 19 (rwb-litigation OUT: TMP Decision: child: approval) and slide 14 (rwb-decision TMP: child: approval); Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 12 note (Approval from the workflow kit, DoA lookup as a parameter), slide 13 note (each stage is a child workflow started on the owner's queue; RouteDecisionWorkflow runs in rwb-valuation 'with ApprovalWorkflow from the kit on rwb-decision'), slide 27 and slide 28 (durable timers, retry policy); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-58 (5 working days, owner Approver at D7.5)
section: Sections 3, 4, 12.5 and 13 of RWB-S4-E5021-APP and sections 11 and 12.5 of RWB-S4-E5021-CON
description: R-LIT-58 gives the petition a 5-working-day answer time and Architecture v5 gives rwb-litigation a child workflow called 'Decision: child: approval', but no source names that child's workflow type, its workflow ID convention, the queue registration beyond 'on rwb-decision', what happens to the petition when the service level expires, or whether the clock is the child's durable timer or a timer of this service. The Temporal design names ApprovalWorkflow as the kit template on rwb-decision for the route decision of S1 and describes the generic Approval template as 'maker-checker, DoA lookup as a parameter'; it never states that the D7.5 petition approval uses the same type. The two stories therefore declare the clock as the approval workflow's and not as their own, name no child type, and carry the mapping as this row.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 19 'TMP Partner: issueInstruction (law firm) - Comms: child: demand notice - Decision: child: approval'; Temporal design slide 12 note 'Approval (maker-checker, DoA lookup as a parameter)'; slide 13 note 'RouteDecisionWorkflow (rwb-valuation, with ApprovalWorkflow from the kit on rwb-decision)'; slide 28 note 'Call fails: activity retry policy 1 s initial interval, back-off 2, 10 attempts' and 'no rule version in force: stops at once'; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-58 'Workbench, Committee View | 5 working days'; no source lists a workflow type per decision point
area: Workflow and timer contract, S4 rwb-litigation with P7 rwb-decision
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P7 rwb-decision architect and the Temporal platform owner
proposed: Name the child workflow type once in the workflow catalogue (the kit's Approval type started on rwb-decision with the decision code of D7.5 as a parameter), fix its workflow ID convention and its queue registration, state whether the 5-working-day service level is the child's durable timer, and point both petition stories at that row instead of at prose.

title: The approval contract publishes no operation that raises an approval item, so the petition's take-to-the-approver shape has no owner
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P7 rwb-decision (Decision and rules)/RWB P7 E2013 CON Approval routing with the delegation of authority table - contract v1.md section 12.1 and its gap CG-B-P7-01-E2013-5; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T-A.1 (API-P7-002 GET /approvals, API-P7-003 approve, API-P7-004 return, API-P7-005 refuse, API-P7-008 GET /approvals/{approvalId}); legacy RWB-E5-021 AC1 ('takes the petition to the approver') and AC2 ('route the petition to the approver at D7.5'); TSD S4 v2 T-A.1
section: Sections 3, 4, 10 and 12.2 of both stories, and the placeholder in section 7 AC2 of RWB-S4-E5021-CON
description: Both stories have to take the petition to the approver at D7.5, and the only approval document of the target is RWB-P7-E2013-CON, which publishes the approval reads and the three decisions and no operation that creates an approval item. That document says so itself and carries the absence as its own gap. The result for this key is that the request shape of the petition's approval is fixed nowhere: the case reference, the decision code, the capability area, the product group, the amount, the source type and reference, the rule and its version and the Idempotency-Key are the elements the approval table of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 gives, and the object that carries them to rwb-decision has no published operation, no field set and no error set. Both stories build against the P7 fake and carry the placeholder rather than invent a path.
evidence: RWB-P7-E2013-CON section 12.1 publishes API-P7-002, API-P7-008, API-P7-003, API-P7-004 and API-P7-005 and states that no operation creates an approval, carrying CG-B-P7-01-E2013-5; TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 lists the same five operations and no raise; TSD S4 v2 T-A.1 lists only the five rwb-litigation operations; the approval item of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 carries DF-DEC-032 to DF-DEC-053 and its owning operation is named by no source
area: Approval contract, P7 rwb-decision with S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: Solution architect, P7 rwb-decision, with the S4 rwb-litigation architect and the API specification owner
proposed: Publish the raise in RWB-P7-E2013-CON as a POST on the decision base with the body the approval row needs, its answer carrying the approval ID, the level, the limit version and the due time, and its error set; until it is published, keep the shape as the consumed stub of the P7 fake and the placeholder in both petition stories.

title: Five values of the petition exist in no source: the bankruptcy test, the approver role at D7.5, the index set of legal_action, the status of a refused petition and the 400 answer
source: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-58 (condition 'enforcement exhausted and the bankruptcy test is met', owner 'Approver at D7.5'); TSD S4 v2 T3.1 (legal_action DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014 and no index row), T3.2 (LOV-LEGAL-STATUS with six values and no refusal value), T6.1 (roles RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-LEGAL, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-HEADLIT and others, none named as the D7.5 approver), T-A.2 (errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503 and no 400); FSD S4 v3 A2.21.3.1 (VR-S4-021-1, R-LIT-58, BR-S4-021 only)
section: Sections 5, 8, 9, 11, 12.1, 13 and 14 of both stories, and the placeholders cited there
description: Five values that both stories need are given by no source read for this key. (1) The bankruptcy test: R-LIT-58's condition names it and no source defines it, so its rows and threshold are unknown. (2) The approver role at D7.5: the rule names 'Approver at D7.5' as the owner and the TSD S4 T6.1 matrix names no role as that approver, so the route code the approval needs is unknown. (3) The index set of legal_action: the TSD gives the columns and the primary key and lists no index, while the workspace read needs a lookup by case_id. (4) The status of a petition refused before filing: LOV-LEGAL-STATUS has six values and none names a refusal, and R-LIT-60 moves the case, not the legal action. (5) The 400 answer: the three S4 T-A.2 rows name 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 and no source names a 400 for a body the service cannot parse. Each is written as the placeholder with this pair rather than guessed.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-58 condition column 'enforcement exhausted and the bankruptcy test is met' and owner column 'Approver at D7.5'; TSD S4 v2 T3.1 has no index or key row for legal_action; TSD S4 v2 T3.2 lists LOV-LEGAL-STATUS as OPEN, FILED, JUDGMENT, ENFORCING, CLOSED, WITHDRAWN; TSD S4 v2 T6.1 lists 30 roles and none is the approver at D7.5; TSD S4 v2 T-A.2 rows API-S4-002, API-S4-003 and API-S4-004 give 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503 and no 400; FSD S4 v3 A2.21.3.1 holds three rows only
area: Business rules, reference data, physical schema and API contract, S4 rwb-litigation with P4 rwb-access and P7 rwb-decision
owner_role: Business analyst and solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P4 rwb-access analyst for the approver role and the DBA for the index set
proposed: Publish the bankruptcy test as reference rule rows with their version, name the D7.5 approver role in the P4 role model and the approval route parameter, add the legal_action index rows to the physical schema note (at least a lookup by case_id), decide the status of a refused petition in LOV-LEGAL-STATUS or state that the row keeps OPEN, and state whether the platform problem document answers 400 for an unparseable body on these three operations.

title: The target gives the matching, the proceeds and the balance application to rwb-payment while the legacy story gives them to S4, and the plan adds no contract dependency for them
source: RWB-E5-022 section 7, section 11 and section 12; FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 A2.22.2 (integration points ALS and GL, LED portal; prerequisite FEAT-PAY-04); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17, 41 and 43; Ownership Map v1 (proceeds owner P8, recovery_case owner P3); plan split slices RWB-S4-E5022-APP and RWB-S4-E5022-CON
description: AC1 and AC3 of the legacy story have S4 match money from the LED or the firm to the case and apply it to the balance, and the legacy data table names proceeds (DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009) as a table this feature writes. The target gives the table proceeds, the activities matchPayments and postProceeds and the ProceedsMatched event to rwb-payment (P8), and it gives recovery_case and the route states CASE_CLOSED and PROCEEDS_MATCHED to rwb-case (P3). The plan therefore gives both slices of this key C = None, while the payment fact can only be read on RWB-P8-E4044-CON Match auction and enforcement proceeds and RWB-P8-E4049-CON Apply proceeds to the case balance, and the case move can only be answered to rwb-case. The legacy dependency FEAT-PAY-04 is a feature row with no story in the plan, so no C row can be derived from it either, and the rwb-case case-move answer has no published operation name in any source.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17 P8 card: "TMP Act: matchPayments, confirmBookings · Act: postProceeds (saga step)" and "DB writes schema rwb_payment: payment and proceeds matching, fees, bookings, posting files"; slide 41 gives S4 "legal actions, hearings, judgments, enforcement, LED auction ladder" and gives P8 "payment and proceeds matching"; Ownership Map v1: proceeds owner P8, recovery_case and legal_action owners P3 and S4; split_plan.json: RWB-S4-E5022-APP and RWB-S4-E5022-CON both carry "C": []; TSD S4 v2 appendix T-A.1 ends at API-S4-005 and names no payment fact and no case move.
area: API
proposed: Keep the metadata as the plan gives it (C = None) and build against RWB-P8-E4044-CON, RWB-P8-E4049-CON and the rwb-case case-move answer with their fakes, one hop and a 2 s budget (ADR-020); add the three rows to the C list of RWB-S4-E5022-APP when the solution architect confirms the owner contracts, and record in the wave 3 harness which legacy balance application maps to which P8 operation.

title: ProceedsMatched does not list rwb-litigation as a consumer, so the payment fact cannot arrive as an event
source: RWB-E5-022 AC1, AC2 and AC3; FSD S4 v3 A2.22.2 step 1 (the trigger is a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 19 S4 IN row, slide 42 and slide 43 event catalogue; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09 and the pattern set of this key
description: The event catalogue gives ProceedsMatched exactly five consumers - rwb-case, rwb-asset, rwb-debtsale, rwb-writeoff and rwb-guarantee - and the S4 IN row of the service card lists only NoticeDelivered and PartnerResultSubmitted, so rwb-litigation is not a consumer of the money event. DP-09 is not in the pattern set of this key either, and the FSD leaves the trigger open as a batch, an event or a timer. The payment fact therefore has to arrive on the P8 owner's contract synchronously, and this story publishes and consumes no event at all, which contradicts the reading of the legacy AC1 and AC3 as a system step fed by an event.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 43 row 25: "ProceedsMatched | rwb-payment | rwb.payment.events.v1 | rwb-case, rwb-asset, rwb-debtsale, rwb-writeoff, rwb-guarantee"; slide 19 notes for rwb-litigation: "IN: REST GET/POST /legal-actions; GET/POST /hearings | events NoticeDelivered; PartnerResultSubmitted | Temporal LitigationWorkflow (years; continues-as-new)"; split_plan.json RWB-S4-E5022-APP patterns: DP03, DP05, DP13, DP19.
area: Event
proposed: Read the matched money on RWB-P8-E4044-CON and RWB-P8-E4049-CON synchronously, declare 12.3 and 12.4 as None in both stories, and keep the catalogue unchanged; if the solution architect later adds rwb-litigation as a ProceedsMatched consumer, one consumed row, one inbox subscription and one fake are added and no schema changes.

title: The legacy story runs unattended while the target trigger is one step of LitigationWorkflow that no source names
source: RWB-E5-022 story statement, AC1 and section 4; FSD S4 v3 A2.22.3.3 and A2.22.4.4; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 19; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 13 and 20
description: The legacy story gives the feature one system step that runs unattended, and the FSD declares no background event, no alternate flow and no named trigger beyond a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer. The target runs the journey in LitigationWorkflow on queue rwb-litigation, whose slide shows steps 5 to 7 (filing and judgment, asset trace and writ, auction at 100/90/80/70 percent) but names no matching step and no start signal. Which step of the workflow owns the evaluation, what starts it, and whether a person can start it as well, are therefore this story's design and not a sourced fact.
evidence: FSD S4 v3 A2.22.3.3: "None; runs unattended | Primary" and "Enforcement owner | Also uses"; A2.22.4.4: "None | No background event"; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 19 notes: "TMP LitigationWorkflow (years; continues-as-new)"; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 20 runs the litigation journey in rwb-litigation / LitigationWorkflow with steps 1 to 7 and the tags System step, Timer, Signal / event, Drools decision, Person, External system, AI agent.
area: Workflow
proposed: Fix the trigger as the arrival of the P8 fact for a case with an open enforcement or LED auction legal action, evaluated in one activity matchEnforcementOutcome of LitigationWorkflow on queue rwb-litigation under the service identity, with no officer task on the happy path and the enforcement owner acting on SCR-20 and on the deferral and approval paths; confirm the step name and the start signal in the RWB-S4-E5022-CON baseline review.

title: The rule rows of R-LIT-51, R-LIT-65 and R-LIT-70 and the D7 approval of a close are governed in rwb-decision but are not listed for this key
source: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-LIT-51, R-LIT-65 and R-LIT-70; TSD S4 v2 T4; FSD S4 v3 A2.22.3.1 and A2.22.4.4; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 27 and 41; Template and Rules v1 R3 default ruling (rule package registry to P7)
description: R-LIT-51, R-LIT-65 and R-LIT-70 are three of the 79 LITIGATION rules over 38 states, and the TSD S4 T4 table stops at R-LIT-25 with 'and 54 more', so the three rows, their version and their test cases are only in the rules workbook and in the registry. area: Rules
proposed: Have rwb-decision publish the three rule rows, their package version and their test cases for the LITIGATION package, and name the approval operation and the limit in the rwb-decision approval contract; until then the app story raises the D7 approval on the published approval contract and waits, and the rule rows are recorded as P7's deliverable.

title: The LED round result, the percentage of official value, the proceeds source code and three operation names have no field or name in any source

DF-LEG-014 status LOV"; RWB-E5-022 section 11: "proceeds | id, case_id, treatment_id, payment_code, source, amount and 3 more | DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009"; TSD S4 v2 appendix T-A.1: API-S4-001 to API-S4-005 only.
area: Data
proposed: Carry the round result, the percentage of official value and the proceeds source code as facts of the RWB-P8-E4044-CON answer only, add no column to legal_action, and mark the three operation names and the element keys that no source gives with the placeholder; fix the field list with the rwb-payment and rwb-case owners in the RWB-S4-E5022-CON baseline review.

title: VR-S4-022-1 tests the freshness of the ACE batch of the source, and rwb-litigation holds no ACE view to test it
source: FSD S4 v3 A2.22.3.1; RWB-E5-022 section 11 (v_ace_account, v_ace_payment); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 29 and 41; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-05
description: The FSD validation rule VR-S4-022-1 tests the freshness of the data product after a late or failed ACE batch for its source and raises MSG-P1-001, reading the legacy v_ace_batch_status. rwb-litigation holds no v_ace_* grant and no grant on rwb_payment (Architecture v5 slide 29), and the ACE view contract, the extension tables and the freshness stamp are P1 rwb-source-data's (slide 41). The rule therefore cannot be evaluated in this service, and no source states which service raises the message for this step or on which contract a freshness answer reaches it.
evidence: FSD S4 v3 A2.22.3.1: "| VR-S4-022-1 | Data product stale after a late or failed ACE batch for its source (v_ace_batch_status) | MSG-P1-001 {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |"; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 29: "rwb-litigation | login rwb_litigation | schema rwb_payment: no grant, refused"; slide 41: P1 owns the ACE view contract and freshness.
area: Data
proposed: Apply VR-S4-022-1 where the ACE data product is read (rwb-payment and rwb-source-data), carry MSG-P1-001 in the message set of both stories and show it on SCR-19 and SCR-20 where the owner reports staleness; add a freshness read to section 12.2 only if the solution architect decides this service must test it itself.

title: The five H rows and two C rows that DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10 and DP-19 add are absent from this story's build and contract lists
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP table); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19, 41 and 44; WP B-S4-05 story line for RWB-S4-E2025-APP (H [] and C [RWB-P5-E2025-CON])
section: Metadata table (Depends on (build), Contract dependencies), section 3 Preconditions, 12.2 REST operations consumed, 12.8 Contract fakes, section 13 Solution plan, section 18 Traceability
description: The DP table adds five H rows to this story's pattern set - RWB-PLT-E1042-CON for DP-06, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON for DP-07, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON for DP-09, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON for DP-10 and RWB-PLT-N001-CON for DP-19 - and two C rows, RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON, for the parameters and reference-data contracts of rwb-case. The plan for this story lists Depends on (build) None and Contract dependencies RWB-P5-E2025-CON only, so the platform parameter and reference-data libraries, the outbox and inbox library, the workflow kit, the composite route and the two rwb-case contracts are named in the pattern table and in the text but are dependencies of nothing. The story cannot read a threshold, a pass mark or a list without them, and it cannot render SCR-19 without the route. The metadata keeps the plan's lists as they stand, the story builds on Day 1 against the five fakes, and two of the five rows (the outbox library and the workflow kit) are not even used by this slice, because it publishes no event and registers no Schedule.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 rows DP-06 'H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON', DP-07 'H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON', DP-09 'H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON', DP-10 'H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON', DP-19 'H RWB-PLT-N001-CON'; WP B-S4-05 story line for RWB-S4-E2025-APP with patterns DP01, DP06, DP07, DP09, DP10, DP11, DP13, DP19, H [] and C ['RWB-P5-E2025-CON']; Architecture v5 slide 41 (rwb-litigation owns legal actions, hearings, judgments, enforcement) and slide 44 (the job map this slice registers nothing in).
area: Litigation (S4) stage 2 and 3 facts: platform libraries, rwb-case parameter and reference-data contracts, edge route
owner_role: Solution architect, with the platform library owners and the rwb-case owners
proposed: Keep the plan's lists as they are, keep the story at Day 1 with RWB-P5-E2025-CON as its only contract dependency, and build against the five fakes. When the platform stories and the two rwb-case contracts publish, add the five H rows and the two C rows to the plan, re-run the dependency check and replace each fake in the same iteration. Two of them (DP-09 and DP-10) are removed from the story's pattern list rather than satisfied, because this slice publishes nothing and schedules nothing.

title: DP-09 and DP-10 are in the pattern list but this slice produces no event, consumes no event and registers no Schedule, and DocumentFieldsExtracted is consumed by rwb-case only
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-09, DP-10); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 19, 42 and 44; legacy RWB-E2-025 sections 12 and 13
section: Section 2 Business rationale, 12.3 Events published, 12.4 Events consumed, 12.6 Schedules, 12.9 Call-type summary, section 13 Solution plan, section 17 Guardrails
description: The story line carries DP-09 (outbox, inbox and CloudEvents) and DP-10 (Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow) because the legacy key is the extraction key, and the extraction is a producer and a scheduled intake. In this slice neither pattern has an application: Architecture v5 slide 42 gives rwb-document event 17 DocumentFieldsExtracted with rwb-case as its only consumer, so rwb-litigation neither produces nor consumes it; the extraction run and the 15-minute intake (JOB-12) and the retention run (JOB-17) belong to rwb-document; and the three events of rwb.litigation.events.v1 - LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded and AuctionResult - belong to the filing, judgment and auction stories, not to a fact fill. The story therefore declares no producer, no consumer, no outbox row, no inbox row, no topic of its own, no cron entry and no Temporal Schedule, and states both rows as prohibitions. No event and no Schedule is invented to give the two patterns an application.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 42 row 17 'DocumentFieldsExtracted | rwb-document | rwb.document.events.v1 | rwb-case'; slide 44 rows JOB-12 'Document intake | every 15 min | rwb-document' and JOB-17 'Retention | monthly | rwb-document | Schedule'; slide 19 'EVT rwb.litigation.events.v1: LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult'; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 rows DP-09 'H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON' and DP-10 'H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON'; legacy RWB-E2-025 section 12 'Event published: DocumentFieldsExtracted (EV-17)'.
area: Litigation (S4) stage 2 and 3 facts: event and schedule scope
proposed: Keep both patterns in the metadata list as the plan gives them and state them as prohibitions in the story: no outbox producer, no consumer, no inbox row and no Schedule in this slice. Remove DP-09 and DP-10 from the pattern list only when the plan is corrected by step D1; until then the story is written so that a build adding an event or a Schedule fails its boundary test.

title: The sources give only the Java interface of the field reader: no REST operation, path, transport or field-level name is named for the checked-fields read
source: Legacy RWB-E2-025 section 12 (DocumentFieldReader and CheckedField); TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 T5.2 and appendix T-A; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (rwb-document contracts)
section: Section 1 Story, section 3 Preconditions, section 4 Flow step 3, 12.1 REST operations provided, 12.2 REST operations consumed, 12.8 Contract fakes, section 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy contract is an in-process Java interface, 'public interface DocumentFieldReader { List<CheckedField> checkedFields(UUID caseId, String documentType); }' with 'CheckedField: documentId, docVersion, fieldName, value, state (OK, CONFIRMED, CORRECTED), confidence'. TSD S4 T5.2 says only that calls go through the published Java interfaces and names P5 for documents, and the TSD S4 appendix T-A lists five S4 operations, none of which is a field read. No source names the HTTP method, the path, the query, the answer wrapper or the field-level names of the target read, so the S4 side cannot fix them: they are fixed by the P5 contract baseline RWB-P5-E2025-CON, which publishes the read on the rwb-document base as its own choice. This story consumes that operation with the legacy shape and builds against its fake, and the placeholder stands wherever the operation is named.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-025 section 12 code block and the note 'The caller passes its own service identity'; TSD S4 v2 T5.2 'Calls go through the published Java interfaces: P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log, P4 for access and reference data, P5 for documents, P6 for notices'; TSD S4 v2 T-A.1 rows API-S4-001 to API-S4-005 (none is a checked-field read); Architecture v5 slide 16 'IN: REST POST /documents ... GET /documents/{id}, /cases/{id}/documents'.
area: Litigation (S4) stage 2 and 3 facts: reader contract transport
owner_role: Solution architect, with the rwb-document owner (P5)
proposed: Fix the read once, in RWB-P5-E2025-CON, as a GET on the rwb-document base with the case and the document type as its parameters and the CheckedField list as its answer, filtered by state and masked by role. This story consumes that operation, keeps the legacy CheckedField element names, adds no second read, and treats the operation name and path as not specified in the source documents until the baseline is tagged.

title: The mapping of an extracted field code onto an S4 column is not stated, and eleven codes, hearing_type and lawsuit_no have no counterpart of the same name
source: TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 T3.1 (legal_action DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014, hearing DF-LEG-024 to DF-LEG-029) and T3.2; legacy RWB-E2-025 section 13 (the five new types and their fields); FSD S4 A2.11 and A2.16
section: Section 1 Story, section 4 Flow step 5, section 7 AC2, section 8 BR1 to BR3, section 11 Data, section 13 Solution plan, section 19 Out of scope
description: The type table version DOCTYPE-2026.12 names the field codes of the six stage 2 and 3 types and TSD S4 T3.1 names the columns of legal_action and hearing, but no source states which code fills which column. Seven pairs share their name and are mapped - court_name, black_case_no, red_case_no, claim_amount, judgment_date, judgment_amount and hearing_date - and the filing date is one recorded name difference, 'filing_date' in the hub against 'filed_date' (DF-LEG-010) in S4. Eleven codes have no S4 column of the same name (contract_no, contract_amount, contract_date, party_names, approval_no, approved_amount, approval_date, approval_level, title_doc_no, mortgage_amount, registration_date, land_office, notice_date), hearing_type (DF-LEG-027) has no extracted code because LOV-HEARING is set by the officer, and lawsuit_no (DF-LEG-005) has no extracted code either. The story therefore maps only the name-identical pairs, writes nothing for the rest, derives no value from one code into a column of another name, and records the difference instead of guessing an amount or a date across two names.
evidence: TSD S4 v2 T3.1 legal_action 'DF-LEG-005 lawsuit_no', 'DF-LEG-006 black_case_no', 'DF-LEG-007 red_case_no', 'DF-LEG-008 court_name', 'DF-LEG-009 claim_amount', 'DF-LEG-010 filed_date', 'DF-LEG-011 judgment_date', 'DF-LEG-012 judgment_amount' and hearing 'DF-LEG-026 hearing_date', 'DF-LEG-027 hearing_type'; legacy RWB-E2-025 section 13 'CONTRACT (contract_no, party_names, contract_amount, contract_date); CREDIT_APPROVAL (approval_no, approved_amount, approval_date, approval_level); MORTGAGE_DOCUMENT (title_doc_no, mortgage_amount, registration_date, land_office); COURT_FILING (court_name, black_case_no, filing_date, claim_amount); JUDGMENT (court_name, red_case_no, judgment_date, judgment_amount); COURT_NOTICE keeps court_name, black_case_no, notice_date and hearing_date'; TSD S4 v2 T3.2 LOV-HEARING.
area: Litigation (S4) stage 2 and 3 facts: field-to-column mapping
owner_role: Business analyst and solution architect, with the rwb-document owner
proposed: Map only the pairs whose names are the same, treat filing_date to filed_date as one mapping recorded as a name difference, and leave the contract, credit-approval and mortgage codes, party_names, notice_date, hearing_type and lawsuit_no unmapped with their gap. If the business needs the contract or mortgage amounts on the action later, that is a new column and a new story, not a silent mapping in code.

title: REQ-DCM-017 and REQ-DCM-018 are in the plan's requirement list for this story but in no row of the legacy traceability table, and legacy section 19 puts them out of scope
source: Legacy RWB-E2-025 sections 18 and 19; Business Requirements Program v4 section 5.5; Business Requirements Epic 2 v2 section 3.5; WP B-S4-05 story line reqs list
section: Section 18 Traceability, section 19 Out of scope, section 7 prose under the gherkin block
description: The plan's requirement list for RWB-S4-E2025-APP is REQ-DCM-006, REQ-DCM-005, REQ-DCM-017 and REQ-DCM-018. The legacy traceability table carries REQ-DCM-006 and REQ-DCM-005 only, and the legacy out-of-scope list names 'Electronic discovery and court evidence attributes (REQ-DCM-017, REQ-DCM-018)'. Both requirements exist in the program and the epic BRD and both are the document hub's: REQ-DCM-017 is the discovery response for a named population with metadata and version history, and REQ-DCM-018 is the set of attributes a court needs to accept a produced document. Neither is a litigation fact and neither is built by this story. The four rows are kept in the traceability table exactly as the plan lists them, each of the two carries the reason it has no test case here, and the difference is recorded rather than resolved by dropping the rows or by asserting a behaviour this story does not have.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-025 section 18 rows REQ-DCM-006 and REQ-DCM-005 only; section 19 bullet 'Electronic discovery and court evidence attributes (REQ-DCM-017, REQ-DCM-018)'; Business Requirements Program v4 row REQ-DCM-017 'The hub answers an electronic discovery request ... Must, Legal counsel, E2' and row REQ-DCM-018 'A document produced from the hub carries what a court needs to accept it ... Must, Legal counsel, E2'; Business Requirements Epic 2 v2 section 3.5 rows REQ-DCM-017 and REQ-DCM-018; WP B-S4-05 reqs ['REQ-DCM-006', 'REQ-DCM-005', 'REQ-DCM-017', 'REQ-DCM-018'].
area: Litigation (S4) stage 2 and 3 facts: requirement traceability
proposed: Keep the four requirement rows as the plan lists them, record for REQ-DCM-017 and REQ-DCM-018 that the legacy table does not carry them and the legacy scope excludes them, and let step D1 decide whether the plan's requirement list or the legacy traceability table is corrected. The discovery response and the court-evidence attributes stay with the document hub's own stories.

title: Several values of the slice are not named by any source: the apply trigger on the patch, its write key, the request element names of the fill, the hearing natural key, the parameter operation names and the composite-route field list
source: TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 appendix T-A.2 (API-S4-002 to API-S4-005 and their Idempotency rows); legacy RWB-E2-025 sections 12 and 13; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 and the platform envelopes
section: Section 3 Preconditions, section 4 Flow, section 7 prose under the gherkin block, 12.1 REST operations provided, 12.2 REST operations consumed, 12.5 Workflows and activities, section 13 Solution plan, section 15 Screens and states
description: The patch operation records 'a filing, judgment or enforcement step' and its Idempotency row says 'Not applicable', while the create and the hearing operations take an Idempotency-Key header. Nothing in the sources says how an officer asks for the checked fields to be applied, what the request element that names the document type is called, what the answer element that lists the applied and the withheld fields is called, what natural key makes one hearing per date, or what the parameters and lists operations of rwb-case are called. The story fixes each of them as its own design so that the build is testable: the document type on the create and on the patch triggers the fill, the write key is derived from the action, the type, the document versions and the values because the patch carries no header, the hearing is unique on the action and the date, and the parameter and list calls are taken from the two contracts and recorded as not specified. The composite-route field list and the merge order stay with the edge contract and are not fixed here.
evidence: TSD S4 v2 T-A.2 'API-S4-002 ... Idempotency | Idempotency-Key header'; 'API-S4-004 ... Purpose | Record a filing, judgment or enforcement step ... Idempotency | Not applicable'; 'API-S4-005 ... Purpose | Add a hearing date ... Idempotency | Idempotency-Key header'; legacy RWB-E2-025 section 13 (no apply operation is described) and section 12 (the reader only); Architecture v5 slide 16 (the rwb-document operations) and slide 20 (producer idempotence).
area: Litigation (S4) stage 2 and 3 facts: operation and element names
proposed: Fix the fill trigger on the create and the patch as the document type in the request, derive the write key from the action, the type, the document versions and the values, make one hearing per action and date a database uniqueness rule inside rwb_litigation, take the parameter and list calls from RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON, and leave the route field list and the merge order to RWB-PLT-N001-CON. Revise the names once when the P5 baseline and the edge contract are tagged.

title: SCR-19 Litigation workspace is listed with its first release in E5, while this story is a wave 2 story released on 31 December 2026
source: FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 Screens table; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (S4 wave 3); WP B-S4-05 story line (wave 2, release 31 December 2026)
section: Section 3 Preconditions, section 7 AC8, section 15 Screens and states
description: FSD S4 lists three screens and gives SCR-19 Litigation workspace its first release in E5, and Architecture v5 gives the rwb-litigation service wave 3, while the story keeps the legacy wave 2 and the release 31 December 2026. The consequence is that the read model this story serves has no screen of its own until the E5 screen work lands. The story therefore builds the panel and its answer against the composite-route fake, proves the read model, and switches the fragment on with the screen. The release date is not raised as a gap and is not changed: it is copied unchanged and marked tentative.
evidence: FSD S4 v3 Screens table 'SCR-19 Litigation workspace | Pack, instruction, court dates, hearings and judgment for a case | E5'; Architecture v5 slide 41 table row 'S4 | rwb-litigation | legal actions, hearings, judgments, enforcement, LED auction ladder | rwb_litigation | /legal-actions | rwb.litigation.events.v1 | rwb-litigation | 3'; WP B-S4-05 story line 'wave: 2, release: 31 December 2026'; Template and Rules v1 R5.6 (a story whose W-MAP wave is earlier than its service's wave keeps the W-MAP wave).
area: Litigation (S4) stage 2 and 3 facts: screen availability
owner_role: Solution architect and the edge owner
proposed: Keep the wave, the release and the screen as the sources give them. Build the read model and the panel against the route fake in wave 2, prove them with the component test, and switch the SCR-19 fragment on with the E5 screen work. No screen, route or release date is invented for this story.

title: No approval of the realigned story or of the sources it consumes is recorded, so the story runs in Draft
source: Legacy RWB-E2-025 document control (Status Ready for build); TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 document control (Status In review); FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 document sign-off
description: The legacy story is at Ready for build, the TSD S4 is at In review and no sign-off row of the FSD, the TSD or the realigned story is filled. This run has no human approval step, so the story is written with Status Draft (realignment v1) and the missing approval is treated as an assumption rather than as a blocker: nothing in the story depends on a signature, and no status of a source document is changed by it.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-025 metadata 'Status | Ready for build' and an empty sign-off table; TSD S4 v2 'Status | In review' and an empty document sign-off table; FSD S4 v3 'Document sign-off' table with no role, name, signature or date; Template and Rules v1 R8.1 and the realignment overlay of D-RCV-60.
area: Litigation (S4) stage 2 and 3 facts: document status and approval
proposed: Carry Status Draft (realignment v1) and record the missing approval as an assumption. Collect the FSD, TSD and story sign-offs in the normal verification loop after this run, and change nothing in the story but its status when they are recorded.
